It made sense for this to be a sub-class back when it was a `ClusterStateUpdateRequest`, but now that it's a regular REST-type request, I think it should live either as a stand-alone class or (since it's pretty small) underneath the action inside of `ModifyDataStreamsAction`. It's definitely irregular to have a request live inside of a service.

Also, we have ModifyDataStream**s**Action and ModifyDataStreamRequest, perhaps we can standardize and go with `ModifyDataStreamsRequest`?

reply.body: Also, once this is a request class in the place we want it, we should add a `ModifyDataStreamsRequestTests` class using `AbstractWireSerializingTestCase` like we do for most of our other requests so we make sure we serialize it correctly

timeline.body:

```suggestion
        this.type = Objects.requireNonNull(type, "[type] must not be null");

I could be missing a valid reason why this couldn't be a constructing object parser though, so let me know if I'm mistaken.

```

> LGTM, I left one really minor comment that doesn't need another review after addressing.

Thanks, @dakrone!

> Out of curiosity, do you think we should (in future work, not time-constrained) support changing which index is the write index of a data stream the same way that we support it for aliases? Does that even make sense for a data stream?

There may be some edge cases in which changing the write index could be useful. Generally speaking, I think it's something that's better avoided since data stream backing indices, under normal usage, will accumulate sequential data in mostly non-overlapping time intervals which facilitates fast retrieval. Allowing arbitrary replacement of the write index could weaken that. It's probably worth a discussion about if we could allow it for the cases where it might be useful without weakening some of the core benefits of data streams.
This description needs an update?
Since this API has a `body` should set `"content_type": ["application/json"]` as well.
Since this API follows very similar construction to `indices.update_aliases` should the `update` verb be used here as well?

reply.body: Thanks, @sethmlarson. I made the above changes in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/79279/commits/50e24f7be5842d4ee2ffb0b4ffc4852ec1fcd771. I wasn't sure what you meant by "using an update verb here"?
Sorry, that was a confusing explanation. I was suggesting the name `update_data_stream` instead of `modify_data_stream`.

Ah, I see. Right now, this API supports only two actions, adding and removing backing indices, both of which could be considered updates, but we have other actions planned for this API that will perform actions that aren't necessarily updates.
